name: Loss and playout simulator
blurb: One voice frame is lost. UDP conceals that one frame; TCP recovers it and holds every frame behind it, and each one whose playout time passes while it waits is lost to the listener anyway.

inputs.label: Frame size
inputs.description: Audio per packet. 20 ms is the usual choice for Opus and for G.711 over RTP.

inputs.label: One-way delay
inputs.description: Milliseconds from sender to receiver, the same for every frame. Acknowledgements take the same time back.

inputs.label: Jitter buffer
inputs.description: How long the receiver waits past a frame's expected arrival before playing it. More buffer absorbs a late repair and adds that much delay to the whole call.

inputs.label: Lost frame
inputs.description: Which frame the network drops, once.

inputs.label: Retransmission timeout
inputs.description: How long TCP waits before resending when no duplicate ACKs arrive. 200 ms is Linux's default minimum; RFC 6298 recommends 1000.

inputs.label: Frames
inputs.description: How many frames the run sends. Fast retransmit needs three after the lost one.
